# NetSec Helm chart

Installs the NetSec operator, its two CRDs (`NetworkIsolation`, `WorkloadHardening`), RBAC and a NetworkPolicy for its metrics port.

The chart was generated by kubebuilder's `helm/v2-alpha` plugin from `make build-installer`, then edited by hand for the values below. Running `kubebuilder edit --plugins=helm/v2-alpha` again overwrites those edits.

## Install

Pass your cluster's context on every command. Your current context may be a real cluster.

```bash
helm --kube-context k3d-netsec install netsec dist/chart \
  --namespace netsec-system --create-namespace \
  --set manager.image.repository=netsec --set manager.image.tag=dev
```

Build the image and load it into the k3d nodes first: `make docker-build k3d-load IMG=netsec:dev`.

## Values

| Value | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `manager.image.repository`, `manager.image.tag` | `controller`, chart `appVersion` | Operator image. |
| `manager.replicas` | `1` | Replicas. More than 1 needs `manager.leaderElection=true`; the chart refuses otherwise. |
| `manager.leaderElection` | `true` | Only one replica acts at a time. |
| `manager.protectedNamespaces` | `[]` | Namespaces never isolated or hardened (`--protected-namespaces`). Empty keeps the built-in default. `kube-*` is always protected. |
| `manager.extraAllowedCIDRs` | `[]` | Single node or tunnel addresses inside the pod range that every policy must still allow (`--extra-allowed-cidrs`), such as flannel's `flannel.1` or Calico's tunnel addresses. A wider block inside the pod range is rejected (`InvalidExtraAllowedCIDRs`). |
| `manager.podCIDRs` | `[]` | Cluster-wide pod range(s) (`--pod-cidrs`), used to keep pod IPs out of the allowed address blocks. Empty uses what Nodes report and marks isolations `Degraded` (`PodRangeFromNodes`). |
| `manager.resources` | 10m/64Mi requests, 500m/128Mi limits | Container resources. |
| `manager.securityContext`, `manager.podSecurityContext` | restricted: non-root, no capabilities, read-only filesystem | Keep these. |
| `metrics.enabled` | `true` | Serve the HTTPS metrics endpoint (needs a token). |
| `networkPolicy.enabled` | `true` | Only namespaces labelled `metrics: enabled` may reach the metrics port. Has no effect when metrics are off. |
| `rbac.helpers.enabled` | `true` | Admin, editor and viewer roles for the two CRDs. |
| `crd.enabled`, `crd.keep` | `true`, `true` | Install the CRDs; keep them on uninstall. |

## Uninstall

Delete your `NetworkIsolation` objects first. Their policies are removed by the operator, so it must still be running.

```bash
kubectl --context k3d-netsec delete networkisolation --all
helm --kube-context k3d-netsec uninstall netsec --namespace netsec-system
```

With `crd.keep=true` the CRDs stay after uninstall (so your objects are not lost). Delete them yourself with `kubectl delete crd networkisolations.netsec.nrnx.dev workloadhardenings.netsec.nrnx.dev`.

`make helm-check` lints, renders, installs, tries a sample isolation and uninstalls on k3d-netsec.
